subject.title: fix(codex): coalesce in-flight dynamic tool calls

question: Should OpenClaw ever collapse two Codex dynamic-tool requests carrying different `callId` values solely because their thread, turn, tool, namespace, and arguments match?
rationale: Codex’s visible protocol path correlates dynamic-tool operations and responses by `callId`; accepting cross-id coalescing changes the meaning of distinct upstream operations and cannot be resolved from the patch’s synthetic duplicate probe.

options.title: Preserve per-call execution
options.body: Keep the existing call-id execution boundary and pursue deduplication only if Codex supplies a distinct replay identity or a demonstrated retransmission contract.

options.title: Adopt cross-id coalescing
options.body: Accept that identical concurrent calls in one turn are semantically one operation and document the intentional suppression of repeated side effects.

recommendation.title: Preserve per-call execution
recommendation.body: Keep the existing call-id execution boundary and pursue deduplication only if Codex supplies a distinct replay identity or a demonstrated retransmission contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed adjacent Codex lifecycle contributor in the supplied current context; ownership remains low-confidence.
